drhp.business: The Company operates an amusement park, water park and associated ride-based attractions at Salt Lake, together with in-park food & beverage, events and banqueting and leased/licensed recreational facilities. Alongside the park, it runs a B2B business providing technical consultancy, project execution and supply of amusement ride components to internal and third-party developments. Its offering spans water rides, dry rides and edutainment for urban and drive-to leisure visitors in the Eastern India catchment.

risks.note: Approximately 1.46 acres was repossessed by the Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal, removing the Eastside Pavilion, Royal Courtyard and Westside Pavilion venues used by the F&B and Other Recreational Facilities segment. The Board's report states that consequent to the discontinuation of operations at these locations, the Company's operational footprint and revenue-generating capacity were adversely impacted - F&B & Other Recreational Facilities revenue fell from Rs. 1,190.52 lakh to Rs. 705.76 lakh and venue-based revenues contracted over 67%. This is a permanent loss of capacity outside management control, and it demonstrates that the Company's operating footprint sits on land it does not fully control.
risks.risk: Land tenure - repossession of leased premises by the state authority

risks.note: Visitor volumes fell to 7.38 lakhs, down 17.6%, and management explicitly characterises the pressure as structural - evolving consumer preferences, increased competition within the existing catchment, and limited recent product refresh impacting repeat visitation. Threats listed include competition from malls, OTT platforms, gaming and live entertainment for discretionary leisure spend. As a single-location destination park, footfall is the primary revenue driver and its recovery depends on new attractions landing with the market.
risks.risk: Structural decline in footfall and competition within the catchment

risks.note: Flagged as the first operational risk - weather dependency and seasonality impacting footfalls - and again under threats as climate variability, with heatwaves, monsoons and weather disruptions affecting park attendance. The Company attributes part of the FY 2025-26 footfall decline to weather-related disruptions. Mitigation rests on diversified attractions, planned shaded zones and heat-resilient attractions, and the all-weather Snow Park targeted for Q3 FY 2026-27, all of which are still to prove out.

Profit before exceptional items fell 49.1% on an 11.0% decline in total income, which management attributes to lower operating leverage arising from reduced volumes and relatively fixed cost structures, adding that inherent cost rigidity continues to influence margins during periods of volume contraction. Threats also cite rising energy, water and maintenance expenses. Earnings are therefore highly geared to footfall in both directions.
risks.risk: Operating leverage and cost rigidity in a volume downturn

risks.note: Management itself cautions that profit after tax growing 5.0% to Rs. 1,969.49 lakhs was supported by exceptional gains during the year and that this improvement is not reflective of the underlying operating performance, underscoring the need to restore core earnings momentum. The gain arose from tendering the Nicco Engineering Services Limited stake into a buyback; on a consolidated basis the same transaction had an adverse impact on profitability. Headline earnings therefore overstate the run-rate.
risks.risk: Reported profit flattered by a one-off exceptional gain

risks.note: Listed as a distinct risk category covering potential ride malfunction or human error and crowd-related security concerns, with threats noting that any operational incident could impact brand perception and regulatory scrutiny. For a brand-led leisure destination a single safety incident is an existential reputational event. Mitigation cited is daily inspections by certified technicians, independent safety checks by global agencies, CCTV surveillance, trained personnel and structured safety protocols.
risks.risk: Guest safety, ride malfunction and reputational exposure

risks.note: Management flags evolving safety, environmental and operational regulations as a risk category, and lists potential changes in taxation, safety norms or environmental regulations under threats. The industry SWOT separately cites a multi-agency compliance load and GST at 18% on park admissions, so a change in the indirect-tax or safety regime would flow straight into pricing or cost.

Flagged as digital platform vulnerabilities and data security risks. The Company's yield strategy depends on online ticketing, cashless in-park transactions and CRM-driven loyalty engagement, and the industry SWOT names dependence on third-party online ticketing platforms as a weakness, so a platform outage or data breach would hit both revenue capture and customer trust.
risks.risk: Technology and cyber exposure on the digital ticketing stack
